"Main premise: 
Open world game where you are an anonymous human and you wander and explore the land and villages, in a country inhabited by primarily anthropomorphic goat people. You start by approaching a village where once you go in you can convene with the inhabitants along with your usual exploration. After talking to some individuals you learn that there has been a problem of a bad group going to villages of these goat people and pillaging the place then kidnapping and enslaving the people, holding them at outposts. You've decided to make it your mission to go to these outposts and liberate the oppressed people through combat with the enemies (who are of different species; not goats). Make it a stereotypical open world rpg, but still somewhat simple so the hero aspect can be the primary focus. 

Goat people's appearance: 
The goats themselves have anatomically correct goat heads with anatomically correct goat eyes that have rectangular pupils. They have horns and either perky goat ears, or pendoulous goat ears. They all have plantigrade legs with human feet that have five toes with fur on the tops of the feet and tops of the toes. They have five fingers. Black fingernails and black toenails. Their palms and soles are furless and are skin colored. They wear an assortment of different clothes while barefoot. 

Game aspects: 
The graphics of the game are photorealistic. Photorealism. Realism. Add AI powered npc communication, so I can have unique conversations with them (the AI of the npcs has a context of their current environment, wherever and whatever that happens to be). Add custom 'per request' actions for the goats (if the player asks, the goat will likely do, such as \"sit down\", or \"lift one leg behind you.\"). Use a publicly available AI for the npc dialogue system.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser RPG about exploring a goat-inhabited country and rescuing captives from a raider outpost.
- Verify the game in a browser and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Include open-world exploration, village conversations, a quest, combat, and captive rescue.
- Goat people should have goat heads, rectangular-pupil eyes, horns, varied ears and clothes, human-shaped five-fingered hands, five-toed plantigrade feet, and no shoes.
- Support open-ended NPC dialogue through a publicly available AI service, with responses informed by the NPC’s environment; provide contextual offline dialogue as fallback.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions and briefly note them upon completion.
- Save and inspect a screenshot as a JPEG no wider than 1280px, reading only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone browser canvas game because the repository had no existing game app or framework.
- AI endpoint, model, and key are configured by the user in settings; offline dialogue remains available without them.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the game interface in `index.html` and responsive styling in `style.css`.
- Implemented world rendering, NPCs, dialogue and action responses, configurable AI requests, movement, combat, quest progression, captive rescue, settings persistence, map overlays, keyboard and touch controls in `game.js`.

4. Summarize the finished work, verification, and assumptions.

- `game.js`: Game engine, rendering, dialogue, controls, combat, quest, and rescue.
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: Game visuals and responsive styling.
- `start.sh`: Local startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.

- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Complete and verify a playable browser RPG about exploring a goat-inhabited country and rescuing captives from a raider outpost.
- Capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot at no more than 1280px wide.

## Requirements
- Include open-world exploration, village conversations, a quest, combat, and captive rescue.
- Goat people should have goat heads, rectangular-pupil eyes, horns, varied ears and clothes, human-shaped five-fingered hands, five-toed plantigrade feet, and no shoes.
- Support open-ended NPC dialogue through a publicly available AI service, with environment-informed responses and contextual offline fallback.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions and briefly note them upon completion.
- Save and inspect a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px, reading only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone browser canvas game because the repository had no existing game app or framework.
- AI endpoint, model, and key are configured by the user in settings; offline dialogue remains available without them.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game interface, world rendering, NPCs and dialogue, AI settings, movement, combat, quest progression, captive rescue, map overlay, keyboard and touch controls.
- Added NPC-spoken quest advancement, captive rendering, and an in-game map.
- Added guarded settings persistence and HTTPS endpoint validation.
- Tested the title screen, movement/location update, settings and map overlays; `node --check game.js` passed before the latest edit.
- Fixed the start-game loading overlay by changing `startGame()` to add the `done` class after 550ms.
- Added a data-URI favicon in `index.html`.

### Active
- Continue browser testing, especially NPC interaction, quest/combat/rescue flow, and touch controls.
- Recapture and inspect the latest JPEG after the loading-overlay fix.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Retest starting the game and confirm the loading overlay disappears after the transition.
2. Verify NPC interaction and progress quest/combat/rescue where practical; test touch controls in a coarse-pointer/mobile context.
3. Run `node --check game.js`, capture a fresh JPEG at ≤1280px wide, and inspect only that latest screenshot.
4. Summarize completed work, verification, and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game engine, rendering, dialogue, controls, combat, quest, and rescue.
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: Game visuals and responsive styling.
- `start.sh`: Local startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Local server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; browser URL is `http://localhost:3002`.
- `playwright-cli` is available. The latest browser check at 390×844 reported touch controls as `display: none`; this was only a viewport resize, not confirmed coarse-pointer emulation.
- Earlier screenshot capture bypassed the start flow and happened before the loading-overlay fix; it does not satisfy the final screenshot requirement.
- A browser console password-field/form warning was observed; the previous favicon 404 should be resolved by the new inline favicon.
